name: Dermatology Skin Tone Fairness Benchmark
description: Addressing fairness in lesion classification from dermatological images is crucial due to variations in how skin diseases manifest across skin tones. However, the absence of skin tone labels in public datasets hinders building a fair classifier. To date, such skin tone labels have been estimated prior to fairness analysis in independent studies using the Individual Typology Angle (ITA). Briefly, ITA calculates an angle based on pixels extracted from skin images taking into account the lightness and yellow-blue tints. These angles are then categorised into skin tones that are subsequently used to analyse fairness in skin cancer classification. In this work, we review and compare four ITA-based approaches of skin tone classification on the ISIC18 dataset, a common benchmark for assessing skin cancer classification fairness in the literature. Our analyses reveal a high disagreement among previously published studies demonstrating the risks of ITA-based skin tone estimation methods. Moreov
reputation: A recent research benchmark for auditing fairness in dermatology skin-tone estimation and lesion classification, but not yet broadly adopted as a standard benchmark.
notes: Non-LLM vision benchmark focused on fairness analysis; results depend heavily on skin-tone estimation method and dataset preprocessing, with substantial methodological disagreement.
